subject: Request: Pin model + EU-only routing for Acme POC
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Routing request for POC - pin model + EU-only

Hi Jonas,

We're getting close to starting the POC next week. Two asks from our security and legal teams that are blocking kickoff: 1) we need inference for the POC to be forced to the `redwood-45b-eu` model (no fallback to other variants), and 2) all traffic must be routed and processed in EU regions only (data residency).

I attached a short requirements doc. Can Redwood support a temporary policy exception for the POC (2-4 weeks) while we complete our procurement review and SOC2 checks? If there are cost or SLA implications please flag them.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Director of AI Platforms, Acme Corp
acme-corp.com

Attachment: acme_poc_requirements.pdf (pdf)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>, Sven Müller <sven.mueller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Routing request for POC - pin model + EU-only

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Looping in Lauren (product) and Karthik (infrastructure) to assess feasibility and any impacts to our routing/fallback policy.

High-level: we frequently support region pinning, but the no-fallback/pinned-model requirement is trickier during capacity constraints — it affects our ability to failover for reliability. We'll follow up with specifics and a proposed safe guardrail for the POC.

Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Routing request for POC - pin model + EU-only

Thanks for the ping. A few product questions to make the scope concrete:

- Is Acme asking that we completely disallow any automatic fallback to smaller/quantized variants, or would a documented, manual fallback only by the customer be acceptable?
- Expected qps and peak concurrency for the POC? That drives whether we can reserve capacity in eu-west.
- Do they require an audit trail for every routed request (audit logs with region + model id) — that adds retention/ingest cost.

If they want a hard pin (no fallback), we'll need an explicit exception ticket and a short SLA addendum noting the risk: if the pinned model is unavailable, requests may fail rather than degrade. We can accommodate for a 2-4 week POC if infra can reserve capacity.

- Lauren
Product Lead, Routing & Runtime

On Fri, Apr 3, 2026 at 09:05 AM jonas_weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the clear ask...
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 13:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Routing request for POC - pin model + EU-only

Quick infra assessment: we can implement a \"pinned_model\" flag that enforces route-to-model and disables automatic fallback for the session. Work items:

- Reserve a small dedicated pool in eu-west-1 for the POC (config + capacity reservation) — estimated 2 x A100 instances for baseline, subject to Acme's qps.
- Add guardrail: optional heartbeat health-checks and short-circuit retry to a standby only in extreme cases (requires legal signoff).
- Logging: we can emit per-request model_id and region; retention configurable.

Risks: pinned-model means higher chance of 503s under overload. We'll need a signed exception acknowledging this risk. Also if reserved nodes are reduced for other customers we can't spill over.

I'll open JIRA-INF-1298 to track changes. Marissa, can you cost this and confirm pricing for reserved short-term pool?

- Karthik
Senior Infra Eng Lead

Cost estimate for a 2-week POC with reserved eu-west pool (approx):

- Reserved infra (2 x A100-equivalent): $12,000/week
- Model licensing delta (redwood-45b-eu q4 usage profile): $3,000/week
- Audit logging extra ingest/retention: $500/week

Total (2 weeks): $31,000 (rounded).

If Acme wants a signed SLA addendum that says we won't fallback, we also recommend a 10% credit holdback in case of availability incidents during the POC — similar to previous exceptions.

Attachment: acme_soc2-exemption-note.pdf (pdf)

- Marissa
Commercial Ops

Jordan — internal alignment complete and next steps below. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a temporary pinned-model + EU routing for the POC with the following conditions: 1) Acme signs an exception addendum acknowledging availability risk; 2) Acme covers the reserved infra and logging costs for the POC period; 3) we set up a short-term ticket (JIRA-INF-1298) and a kickoff call Monday to finish sizing and ACLs.

Proposed next steps:
- Jordan/Sven: confirm qps/expected concurrency and confirm acceptance of the exception terms (we'll share the addendum).
- Marissa: send formal quote and DocuSign link for the POC reservation.
- Karthik: reserve eu-west-1 pool and enable pinned_model flag for the Acme tenant; provide runbook for on-call.
- Lauren: create a one-page product note describing the behavior (no automatic fallback) to share with Acme's legal/security teams.

I'll schedule the Monday call and attach the proposed addendum. Thanks all — looks like a small amount of engineering and a short commercial commitment to keep the POC on track.

Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
